\chapter{More Everyday Verbs}
\label{ch:ml-more-verbs}
\hlchaptermodality{43}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can tell someone to come, sit, stand and give in Malayalam.}

Complete ML-C43-give and say all four verbs in order.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[ōṭū]{\ml{ഓടൂ} (ōṭū) — run}

\label{lesson:ML-C43-run}



\begin{quote}
A short run of everyday verbs, one at a time.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഓടൂ}}
\textbf{\ml{ഓടൂ}} (\emph{ōṭū}) — \textquotedblleft{}run\textquotedblright{}.

The long final \emph{ū} softens a command into an invitation — Malayalam marks courtesy in the verb ending itself.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more everyday action. Three more follow, and each reuses the ones before it.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{ōṭū}
  \item it again, to someone standing in a doorway
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഓടൂ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}run\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[uṟaṅṅū]{\ml{ഉറങ്ങൂ} (uṟaṅṅū) — sleep}

\label{lesson:ML-C43-sleep}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{ōṭū} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഉറങ്ങൂ}}
\textbf{\ml{ഉറങ്ങൂ}} (\emph{uṟaṅṅū}) — \textquotedblleft{}sleep\textquotedblright{}.

Same softening vowel — said to a child at night rather than as an order.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more everyday action. Three more follow, and each reuses the ones before it.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{uṟaṅṅū}
  \item it again, to someone standing in a doorway
  \item it after \emph{ōṭū}, so the two sit together
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഉറങ്ങൂ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}sleep\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[tarū]{\ml{തരൂ} (tarū) — give}

\label{lesson:ML-C43-give}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{nilkkū} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{തരൂ}}
\textbf{\ml{തരൂ}} (\emph{tarū}) — \textquotedblleft{}give\textquotedblright{}.

'Give — to me.' Malayalam distinguishes giving toward the speaker from giving away; this is the toward-me one.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more everyday action. That closes the run: four everyday actions, each met on its own.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{tarū}
  \item it again, to someone standing in a doorway
  \item it after \emph{nilkkū}, so the two sit together
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{തരൂ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}give\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
